name: Jackson §14.8: Thomson scattering
description: Jackson §14.8: a light wave (coming from the right, ω = 1) shakes a charge, and the shaken charge radiates: it scatters the light. A charge flying into the wave meets its crests faster, and moving towards the receiver it squeezes what it sends there: heading at $\varphi$ against the wave, it is seen at an angle $\theta$ to scatter $\omega_s = \omega\,\frac{1 + \beta\cos\varphi}{1 - \beta\cos(\theta - \varphi)}$, up to $\omega_s \approx 4\gamma^2\omega$ head on: how laser light is turned into X-rays (inverse Compton sources). The receiver at 30° counts only 27–33: steer the particle so that the light it scatters towards the receiver lands in that band, at least 0.003 per steradian.

reality.represents: Thomson scattering of light by a fast charge: inverse Compton (Jackson §14.8)

remarks.detail: A charge flying into a light wave meets it faster and sends the scattered light forward squeezed: how laser light becomes X-rays in inverse Compton sources.

remarks.line: The radiation is exact for the motion
remarks.detail: What the receiver collects is computed from the particle's computed path with the exact far-zone fields (Liénard; the spectrum from Jackson's radiation integral), and the particle feels its radiation's reaction (Landau–Lifshitz).

Classical scattering leaves out the Compton recoil, valid while the light's photon energy, seen from the charge, is far below its rest energy; at higher energies the recoil lowers the scattered frequency.
The receiver averages over directions in the plane of the motion; the real radiation also goes out of the plane, where its pattern differs.
